biggest_gap.what: The RI-WPN05 impact and material model is a data island, exactly as the 87 movesets were in round 1. Five of six perturbations of the shipped tables change nothing in the fight: setting every non-flesh cell of the 5x7 attacker hitstop grid to 99 f, setting every material damage multiplier to 0.01, setting every knockback value to 9 m, and setting the deflection multiplier to 20x all produce a byte-identical fight (dmg 118, hit at frame 32, hitstop held 3 frames). Only the flesh column is read, and it is read from a hard-coded `.flesh` lookup at game/src/combat/moves.js:166. MovesetLibrary.materialMultiplier, .deflects, .knockbackFor and .victimHitstopFor are imported by exactly one file in the repository — game/src/harness/weapons.js, the harness. And there is nothing for them to apply to: 0 of the 14 enemy statblocks in game/data/combat/enemies/ declares a material at all. The hard-coded lookup is game/src/combat/moves.js:166 — `hitstop_frames: (s.hitstop_f || lib.classes.hitstop.attacker[moveset.weight_tier] || {}).flesh || 6` — and a grep for materialMultiplier|deflects|knockbackFor|victimHitstopFor across game/src/ returns only game/src/harness/weapons.js.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: This is round 1's verdict repeating itself one layer down, and it is invisible for the same reason: the builder fixed the half of the piece the round-1 gap named and the impact half was never examined, so every probe that reads the library reports a healthy 5x7 grid. From the player's chair a mace, an axe and a spear hit a stone golem, a chitin-shelled beast and a Hist-bonded plant creature with identical feedback — same hitstop, same knockback, no deflection, no damage-type advantage. The material system is also this area's ONLY seam crossing under AR-3: a lore fact (root-golems are stone, the Hist-bonded are plant) that is supposed to be a combat answer a merchant can sell you. Unread, the crossing does not exist, and the weapon area becomes internally excellent and externally sterile.

remedy.action: Make the fight read the material at hit time, and give it a material to read.
targets: game/data/combat/enemies/*.json — add a `material` (one of flesh, chitin, stone, metal, plant, water, wood) to all 14 statblocks; the lore assignment is already written down in RI-WPN05 B.

game/src/combat/resolve.js — at the frame a hit resolves, look the victim's material up and call MovesetLibrary.hitstopFor / victimHitstopFor / knockbackFor / materialMultiplier / deflects, instead of consuming the pre-baked move.hitstop_frames.

secondary_observations.what: The interior dead bands are attributable to this piece, and the W1-09 round-3 builder's attribution is correct. The gap moves with root_dz_m (0 -> none, 0.20 -> [0.95,1.45], 0.575 -> [1.30,1.60], 0.80 -> [1.50,1.70], 1.20 -> none) and with the clip's capsule_length_m, both W1-10-owned. The mechanism is game/data/weapons/classes.json's hitbox_span_m: SPR declares 0.70 m of hit volume on a 2.70 m capsule, so only the outer quarter of the shaft can damage, and a target standing in the shaft band is inside the blade and outside the S26 body corridor. It is not confined to spear and halberd — axe_bog_cleaver has one too, and the same span values are why AXE, GHM, HLB, MCE and SPR all fail reach_min_m <= 0.60.

Declared reach is not the reach the game produces, and the fingerprint is built on the declared column. HLB declares 2.865 m and its blade reaches 1.45 m; CGS declares 2.75 and reaches 1.40; TSW declares 2.087 and reaches 0.95; GSW 2.741 -> 1.75; UGS 3.033 -> 2.35. The tolerance is +/-0.10 m. Measured melee blade-reach spread is 1.90 m against a required 2.5, and threat_m spread 2.05 m against a required 3.0 — both PASS on the declared numbers and FAIL on the measured ones.

Round 1 observed 'recovery arc exceeds active arc in 7 of 14 movesets'. It is now 21 of 28 driven clips, and in several cases by a wide margin — MCE r1.1 sweeps 114 degrees while its hitbox is live and 330 after it switches off; UGS r2 sweeps 130 active and 341 in recovery. The visible swing and the damaging window have come apart, which is a legibility defect a player reads as a hit that should have landed.

Dg_min PASSES, and the builder was right to file arithmetic rather than curve-fit. Under the bar critic's repaired nine-dimension GRAMMAR_DIMS over 14 melee classes the roster measures Dg_min 1.5981 observed and 1.7272 declared against a 1.0 bar, without a line of the roster being changed. Under the superseded five-dimension set the same roster measures 0.628 observed. The instrument was wrong, not the design. Recorded so the refusal to curve-fit is on the record as correct.

All ten CGS and GHM weapons declare r1.3 and reach it via roll.r1 -> r1.3 and backstep.r1 -> r1.3. RI-WPN01 A as amended wave 1 publishes roll.r1 -> r1.2 and states that this workaround 'is not adopted'. The amendment's mtime is 22:26 and the builder's commit is 22:11, so this is a rule created fifteen minutes after the build, not a rule the builder ignored. Recorded as a live nonconformance with that timing stated.

plunge is one of the mandatory 25 and is unreachable in every shipped fixture: no state file in game/data/states/ produces a fall of the 3.0 m the slot requires, so a 51-frame sweep of the jump on four weight tiers never resolves it. It is declared on all 87 weapons.

Four of the twenty CFS instances — the whole BLOCK row — resolve to shield.bash playing shield_bash_medium, byte-identically on all four probe weapons. That is correct under RI-WPN06 C, because shield.bash belongs to the offhand, but it means a fifth of the headline contextual score is measuring the shield rather than the weapon. Worth a companion clause in RI-WPN04.

Over twelve runtime blind traces of about ten scripted attacks each, against a STATIONARY dummy at 2.2 m, hit counts run 0 to 4 and two traces (spr_reed_gig, ghm_stone_breaker) land nothing at all. No number in the seven asks how often a scripted swing at a motionless target at ordinary spacing connects, and the answer is: less than half the time.
getBuildInfo().piece still reads 'W1-09 — combat core' and version '0.2.0-w1-09'. The build stamp was not advanced in round 1 and has not been advanced in round 2.

arbitration_questions.question: Does an authored model that no code path outside the harness reads make a piece seam_sterile under AR-3, even though the model itself is present and correct?
arbitration_questions.position: Yes, and this verdict applies that reading. ARBITRATION 3's CONSUMPTION clause already says that from the player's chair a model with no demonstrated consumer and a missing model are the same thing. AR-3 asks whether the piece carries an interaction that crosses the seam; an interaction nothing performs is not carried. Recorded as an arbitration question rather than assumed, because AR-3's text speaks of the interaction being 'declared rather than exercised' as a lesser state, and this is the second round running that this area has been scored on that basis.

self_audit.notes: Ladder rungs used, in order. (1) Ran the seven headline numbers with my own instruments and found CFS_live, equipped_ok, ARI, TDV, Dg_min and the moveset CONSUMPTION check all genuinely passing — round 2's headline claims survive independent measurement. (2) Changed the sample, per WEAPON-CRITIC 8's known good rung: went to the classes with the largest lunges and the smallest hit spans rather than the ones the probes demo, which is where the S26 contiguity hard fail was. (3) Stopped trusting the declared column and measured arc, reach and root off the rig, which is where 24 of 28 arc mismatches and the 1.42 m halberd reach error were. (4) Re-ran the round-1 gap's own detector one layer down — asked which OTHER model in this piece is imported only by the harness — which is where the biggest gap was. Two builder-authored instruments (tools/weapons/verify-frames.mjs and tools/harness/wpn-census-live.mjs) were deliberately never executed; every number in this verdict comes from a tool written for this review or from the game itself.
self_audit.self_audit_note: ran_every_assigned_method is FALSE and this is why. Four methods were not run and each is recorded as a check with result 'unmeasurable', scored 0 fail-closed per CRITIC-DOCTRINE §7.3 rather than skipped: RI-WPN04 M5 (situational superiority — no fixture set exists in which a contextual slot can be shown to be the right answer; unrun in round 1 too, and BAR-CRITIQUE-W1-10-R1 §H2 names it as the one quality bar in this area that has never been run); RI-WPN06 M5 (the O2 dual-wield configuration equips but was not driven to a landed off-hand hit); RI-WPN03 M3's SEP (the F87 fingerprint was not recomputed under the amended D5, and round 1's 1.4469 is not carried over because BAR-CRITIQUE-W1-10-R1 §R1 shows it was read off a reach column with 85% of its discrimination normalised away — reported as NOT RUN rather than as a stale number); and RI-WPN07's RVS plus RI-WPN03 §D.3's Chg_min, both of which are items created by the concurrent bar-critic pass DURING this review and after the build was made — recorded as wave-2 debts per the orchestrator's instruction not to retro-penalise. None of the four affects the verdict, which is decided by three hard fails that were measured: S26 contiguity, the impact/material model's absent consumer, and the E.2 pose teleport. The verdict is provisional to that extent and the four gaps are named so a successor runs them rather than rediscovers them.

notes.seam_sterile_justification: This area's only declared seam crossing is RI-WPN05 B's material system, and it is authored and unread: 0 of 14 enemy statblocks carries a material, materialMultiplier is imported only by the harness, and zeroing every material multiplier changes no damage. A lore fact that is supposed to be a combat answer currently answers nothing. Round 1 recorded this as 'declared rather than exercised' and scored seam_sterile false; that was too generous and this verdict corrects it.

bar_pressure.q1_is_a_passing_score_the_thing_the_user: Not yet, and the honest answer changed shape this round. Taken at random, hlb_saltcutter differs from its class baseline by a longer sweep and a 0.495 m lunge — and a player cannot feel either, because the halberd's blade reaches 1.45 m against a declared 2.865 and has a hole in the middle of the band. The user asked for weapons that are subtly unique in the hand. The roster IS subtly unique on paper and the two channels through which a player would feel it — where the weapon reaches, and what it feels like when it lands — are the two that are broken. The bar is right; it is now measuring the right thing for the first time, which is why the score fell rather than rose.
bar_pressure.q2_which_threshold_does_no_work: SEP. Its within-class ceiling is dominated by whichever pair of same-class weapons happens to share the most clips, and the SHARE cap already bounds that from above, so SEP is largely a restatement of ARI with a different denominator. It has never been the deciding number in either round. Proposed replacement: report SEP over the OBSERVED F87 only, and add a companion floor on the second-nearest between-class distance so one well-separated pair cannot carry it.
bar_pressure.q3_which_threshold_is_gameable_and_how_c: arc_sweep_deg, and this round proves it is not hypothetical — it is already wrong. D6 and G3 are read from a declared JSON field that 24 of 28 clips do not honour, so `sed -i 's/"arc_sweep_deg": 19/"arc_sweep_deg": 340/'` across the SPR movesets would move D_min, Dg_min and the M5 shape census without changing a frame of animation. The companion check is already written for reach and must be extended: RI-WPN02 M3 must read arc from the hitbox records, never from the declaration, exactly as M1-C now reads reach. That is my concrete proposed amendment.
bar_pressure.q4_the_tenth_hour_version: A player ten hours in complains that swings that visually connect do not damage. Nothing in the seven numbers asks how often a swing at a stationary target at ordinary spacing lands, and the blind pack answered it by accident: 0 to 4 hits from about ten scripted attacks per trace, and two of twelve traces landing nothing at all. Proposed new measure, `CR` (connect rate): the fraction of scripted r1.1 presses that damage a stationary dummy placed at the class's own declared reach minus 0.20 m. Floor 0.95. It is one line of harness work and it would have failed this build in round 1.
bar_pressure.q5_is_the_roster_the_right_size: Yes, and more confidently than round 1 could say it. ARI 0.4533 sits mid-band under the amended floor, the share histogram tops out at four, and the runtime motion-only blind pack — a far harder test than round 1's — still separated one class of three perfectly and named four real within-class behavioural differences. The remedy is not fewer weapons. It is the same weapons with hit volumes that match their blades and impact that reads the thing it hits.

proposed_amendment.replacement_text: D6 `arc_sweep_deg` — total angular travel of the hitbox capsule's midpoint about the player's Y axis across the ACTIVE window, **measured from the hitbox records of a driven attack and never read from the moveset declaration**, computed with a near-axis guard (frames whose horizontal radius from the root is below 0.20 m are excluded) and cross-checked against the tip's angular travel; where the two estimators differ by more than 15 degrees the slot is reported as unmeasurable rather than scored. The same discipline S26 imposes on reach applies here: a geometry dimension inferred from a declared value is not a measurement. **FAIL** if more than 2 of the 14 melee class baselines' `r1.1` arcs differ from their declaration by more than 10 degrees — this build measures 24 of 28 driven clips outside tolerance while the declared column passes every check.

second_proposed_amendment.replacement_text: `ILS` is computed over the 35 cells by requiring that each cell's observable triple (attacker_hitstop, camera_shake_peak, knockback_m) be **unique across the grid**; a cell whose triple is shared with any other cell is not recovered. The previous wording specified a nearest-neighbour classifier, which over 35 distinct points recovers zero by construction and made the headline number unrunnable as written. `ILS` is scored on the OBSERVED grid only — a grid computed by calling the library rather than by reading it out of a trace against a material-carrying target is `unmeasurable => 0`.

sampling.rule: Stratified and adversarial per WEAPON-CRITIC 3.2. Full population (87) for equip, ARI, TDV and the schema census. All 15 class baselines for the fingerprint, motion, arc and reach censuses. All 13 SPR and HLB weapons for the contiguity attribution. The four weight-tier probes (dagger, straight-sword, axe, ultra-greatsword) for the Wgrid, the airborne sweep and the browser parity check. Twelve traces across GHM/SPR/TSW and three across CSW/HLB/MCE for the blind tests.

notes.what_survived_the_harsh_lens: Recorded because CRITIC-DOCTRINE 2.1 requires the ladder to be visible and because five checks that could have caught this build did not. The 87 movesets really are in the game: 87/87 equip in the shipping browser build, CFS_live is genuinely 1.0000 with distinct slot, clip and frame triple on all twenty instances, jump.r1 and backstep.r1 genuinely fire, seven of seven perturbations of the moveset model change the fight, node and browser agree on every cell I compared, AR-1 is clean on 60 identical swings and eight cancellation tests, TDV is real motion and not a multiplier, and Dg_min passes the repaired instrument without the roster being touched. Round 2 did what it said it did. The gap is somewhere else.
